summary.oneLiner: Differentiated upper-upscale hotel chain (91% occupancy, RevPAR leadership) crossing the ₹700cr revenue milestone, doubling keys to 6,635 by FY30 via a heavy owned + 3x asset-light pipeline, with a separately scaling Flurys F&B retail engine (110→140+ outlets) and embedded real-estate (EM Bypass Kolkata) unlocking cash flow. Near-term earnings dragged by Middle-East-war cancellations, higher depreciation/interest from expansion, and acquisition financing (Zillion).

thesis (one-liner): Differentiated upper-upscale hotel chain (91% occupancy, RevPAR leadership) crossing the ₹700cr revenue milestone, doubling keys to 6,635 by FY30 via a heavy owned + 3x asset-light pipeline, with a separately scaling Flurys F&B retail engine (110→140+ outlets) and embedded real-estate (EM Bypass Kolkata) unlocking cash flow. Near-term earnings dragged by Middle-East-war cancellations, higher depreciation/interest from expansion, and acquisition financing (Zillion).
scorecard (consolidated): One-offs / non-recurring: EM Bypass Kolkata service-apartment sales — 29 of 34 apartments in Block 1 sold at avg ₹20,857/sqft; cash flow +₹11 cr up to Apr'26, expecting ~₹70 cr additional cash flow this year (total ₹350 cr expected from EM Bypass over project). FY26 PAT hit by Middle-East war cancellations + higher depreciation + ₹7 cr higher interest (mainly Zillion acquisition financing charged to P&L). No normalized PAT given by mgmt — reported figures only.
guidance (critical): Keys: 2,677 keys (42 hotels) now → >3,000 keys by FY27 (add 12 hotels / 472 keys in FY27, 8 of which asset-light → 3,149 per dev slide); 6,635 keys (85 hotels) by FY30. Owned ~2x, asset-light (Zone/Zone Connect) ~3x over 4 years.

RevPAR/ARR: ARR is "prime focus" growth lever (occupancy near-ceiling). Renovations at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Vizag + premiumization (200+ room super-luxury formats) to lift ARR; demand-supply gap (~200-300 bps supply shortfall) supportive.

Flurys outlets: 110 → +30 outlets over next 10 months (Delhi NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4; West Bengal/Hyderabad) → ~140+; +40-50 outlets over next 4 years to 2030; target 100 outlets in West Bengal alone by 2027 centenary. FY26 Flurys revenue +29% YoY.
Margin: "sustained margin improvement" guided; interest cost expected to stay at/below 8.35% MCLR; project-finance interest to be capitalized as IDC (not P&L), keeping P&L "under control."
Top line: mid-teens prior guidance; FY26 delivered 12% (mgmt defends as good given 2 disruptions); expects current quarter to be "good and stable."
pipeline (keys / outlets): EM Bypass Kolkata: integrated mixed-use — 218 hotel rooms + 69 service apartments; Block 1 launched (29/34 apts sold ₹20,857/sqft); Block 2 launch Sep-Oct'26 (festive).
Park Mumbai @ Juhu: design finalized, now 78 rooms; construction starts Jun'26, completion ~Mar'27.
Vizag: 100-room dev; env clearance now in place; on-ground launch Aug'26; opening pushed to early 2030 (was early 2029) due to permission delays (no basement → may accelerate).
Pune: 250+ rooms planned. Navi Mumbai: additional 3.8 lakh sqft FSI → 250 rooms planned. Jaipur: in 5-project list.
FY26 launches: 7 properties / 283 keys, incl. Q4: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect Gangtok, Zone Connect Katra.

Acquisitions: Malabar House Cochin (Relais & Chateaux, high-ARR, FX/RBI permission now granted, close by June, put in Q2); Purity Cochin (17-room Vembanad Lake, operated only 3 months in FY26); Zillion & THALI (~₹330 cr acq/project cost); 3 lease properties to acquire FY27; Luxmi Tea asset-light Park brand at Siliguri signed. West Bengal 400 rooms to double over 4 years.
segment (owned / managed / flurys): Owned/leased hotels: core driver; Park Calcutta (149 rooms) 100% occupancy, T-RevPAR ~₹24,000 (highest in CBD, beats luxury brands), beverage revenue > room revenue most months. Patiala (Ran Baas) FY ARR ₹31,000+ (~20% occ, targeting ~50% in Oct-Dec season); Lotus Palace Chettinad ARR ~₹12,000 (~30% occ).
Leased (336 keys): blended ARR/occ not given (to be emailed). Individual: Zone Connect Saket ~₹7,000; Chettinad ₹12,000; Patiala ₹31,000.
Asset-light (Zone/Zone Connect): 3x growth engine to FY30; Siliguri (Luxmi Tea) signed.
F&B: crossed ₹300 cr in FY26 = ~43% of total revenue (among highest in industry); restaurants, nightlife, experiential dining.
Flurys: 110 outlets, +29% revenue YoY FY26; new COO Rohit Kakra (ex-Costa Coffee, Pizza Hut, 23 yrs) from Apr'26.
growth / optionality (asset-light, flury: Asset-light Zone/Zone Connect targeted 3x to FY30 — capital-light keys growth; 8 of 12 FY27 hotels asset-light.

Flurys central-kitchen pivot (KEY): dropped plan for own central kitchen in Delhi (would've cost ₹20-30 cr + long build); now outsourcing manufacturing to a vendor (agreement signed) — asset-light on both store AND production level → faster multi-metro rollout (Delhi, Bangalore, Pune). Recipes/craftsmanship preserved with QC chefs at vendor sites.
Embedded real-estate monetization (EM Bypass apartments) as recurring cash-flow lever.
Nor1 AI-driven upselling platform; SAP S/4HANA implemented FY26; "AI-first" org.
margins & cost: FY26 EBITDA margin 30.82% (Q4 28.85%); mgmt guides sustained margin improvement.
Cost headwinds flagged: LPG shortages select markets, inflationary operating costs, higher depreciation + finance costs from expansion.
F&B/banqueting + nightlife (high-margin beverage) supports T-RevPAR premium vs peers.
capex: ~5 projects (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur) = ~950 rooms @ ~₹1.2 cr/room ≈ ₹1,100 cr (less EM Bypass contribution of ₹350 cr).
Normal/maintenance capex ~₹40 cr p.a.; Flurys ~₹30-40 cr p.a.
Total funding demand ≈ ₹1,500 cr, funded mostly via internal accruals (assuming ~₹250 cr EBITDA over 5 yrs); cash & equiv ~₹80 cr + line of credit.
capital allocation: 75% dividend payout approved by board (mgmt frames as balance-sheet strength signal).
Funding skewed to internal accruals + EM Bypass real-estate cash flows; project interest capitalized as IDC to protect P&L.
Acquisition financing (Zillion) charged to P&L (₹7 cr interest hit FY26).
risks: Geopolitics: Middle-East war + Operation Sindoor (Q1) caused significant Delhi & Hyderabad cancellations; ceasefire still unsettled at call time.
Flurys execution risk on outsourced manufacturing — maintaining brand quality differentiation; prior guidance miss on outlet count (FY26 ended lower than guided).
High base on ARR/RevPAR; occupancy near ceiling limits volume-led growth.
Capital-intensity / rising depreciation & finance costs during heavy build-out.
Small avg property size (~100 rooms) vs larger peers (300-room) — mgmt counters with T-RevPAR/F&B mix.
mgmt tone: Confident, defensive on the 12% (vs mid-teens) miss — repeatedly attributes to two external disruptions; bullish on Kolkata (govt change → investment, real estate, demand-supply gap). Candid on Flurys central-kitchen reversal and outlet-count shortfall. Some Q&A friction (analyst pressing on Park Calcutta "100% occupancy" methodology; mgmt deflected). Leased ARR/occ not readily available (to be emailed).
non-obvious: Park Calcutta beverage revenue > room revenue in most months; T-RevPAR ~₹24,000 (CBD-leading) despite only 149 rooms & upper-upscale (not luxury) positioning; 30% repeat customers.
F&B = ~43% of revenue (crossed ₹300 cr) — unusually high F&B mix differentiates from pure-room peers.
Flurys 2027 centenary year → 100-outlet West Bengal target as brand event.
Branded room supply in India only ~2,16,000; Kolkata only 5,101 keys with ~1,702 added over 5 yrs — structural pricing tailwind.
Pivot to 200+ room super-luxury formats (vs historic ~100-room) is a strategic positioning shift up-market.
challenges → beneficiaries: ⭐ Branded-room demand-supply gap (esp. Kolkata, premium metros) → benefits established branded operators like PARKHOTELS.
✅ Middle-East-war international-travel disruption → mgmt positions as domestic-demand beneficiary (strong domestic player).
F&B-retail/cafe formalization tailwind → Flurys scale-up (outsourced mfg model).
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Rev ₹184cr (+4% YoY), EBITDA ₹53cr (28.85%), PAT ₹12cr. FY26 Rev ₹707cr (+12%), EBITDA ₹218cr (30.82%), PAT ₹66cr, Occ 91%, ARR ₹8,304 (+9%), RevPAR ₹7,584 (+7%). 75% dividend. Keys 2,677/42 hotels → 6,635/85 by FY30. Flurys 110 outlets (+29% rev), central-kitchen → outsourced mfg pivot. EM Bypass apt sales (+₹11cr cash, ~₹70cr expected). Vizag pushed to 2030. Malabar House acq closing June. New Flurys COO (Rohit Kakra). Two disruptions (Op Sindoor Q1, Mid-East war Q4) drove Delhi/Hyderabad cancellations & 12% (vs mid-teens) FY top-line.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
